description: Plan-runner tears down its planner/auditor pane on every terminal (incl. non-audit post-spawn), closing the residual mutex-busy lingering-pane gap.

userStories.title: Tear down plan panes at a single unconditional exit in runPlanPhaseWithReplan
userStories.description: As the cam supervisor, I need runPlanPhaseWithReplan to tear down the planner/auditor pane on EVERY terminal return (not just audit-approved and plan-escalated) so that non-audit post-spawn terminals (planner-timeout, auditor-timeout, planner-failed) no longer leave a live claude TUI holding paneCountMutex busy and forcing a manual kill.
acceptanceCriteria: runPlanPhaseWithReplan invokes the teardownPlanPanesFn seam on every terminal return path, including the non-audit post-spawn terminals (planner-timeout, auditor-timeout, planner-failed) that currently fall through to the plan-runner.ts return with no teardown. Teardown is applied at a single unconditional exit point (drift-proof, mirroring the worker finishTerminal-always-tears-down invariant) rather than by enumerating terminal kinds. [oracle: bun test test/supervisor/plan/plan-runner-replan.test.ts]

Pre-spawn terminals (preflight-failed, no-plannable-issue, plan-target-invalid, mutex-busy, container-preflight-failed) also pass through the exit-teardown as a harmless no-op (kill-pane is best-effort when no plan pane exists); they return the same result kind as before. [oracle: bun test test/supervisor/plan/plan-runner-replan.test.ts]

The CAM-204 round-boundary teardowns (the teardown() call between re-plan rounds, plan-runner.ts:878) are preserved unchanged, and the final exit-teardown never kills a pane a subsequent re-plan round would reuse (the exit-teardown fires only at function exit, after the re-plan loop has completed). [oracle: bun test test/supervisor/plan/plan-runner-replan.test.ts]

A test drives runPlanPhaseWithReplan to a planner-timeout (and separately to auditor-timeout and planner-failed) and asserts teardownPlanPanesFn was invoked exactly once for that terminal, so the tmux session drops back to 2 panes and paneCountMutex reads available for the next cam plan/next/ship. [oracle: bun test test/supervisor/plan/plan-runner-replan.test.ts]

The existing sidecar wiring (makeTeardownPlanPanesFn passed as teardownPlanPanesFn, sidecar.ts:2249) is unchanged and still exercised on the non-audit terminals. [oracle: bun test test/supervisor/plan/plan-sidecar-replan-wiring.test.ts]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Lint spine passes (bun run check:all). [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: Single-file core-logic fix. Primary edit: src/supervisor/plan-runner.ts runPlanPhaseWithReplan (lines ~864-928). The teardown seam (teardownPlanPanesFn) and its real wiring (makeTeardownPlanPanesFn, src/commands/sidecar.ts:1969 + 2249) already exist from CAM-204; do NOT re-implement or re-wire them. Only close the residual gap: today teardown() runs on audit-approved (887) and plan-escalated (914) but the final non-audit fall-through return (927) skips it. Prefer restructuring to a single unconditional exit teardown (e.g. compute the terminal result then teardown once at the sole exit, or a try/finally whose finally calls teardown) so that a future post-spawn terminal kind cannot re-open the gap (enumeration is exactly how AC5 originally missed planner-timeout/auditor-timeout/planner-failed). Keep the in-loop round-boundary teardown at 878 as an explicit mid-function call (it is not an exit). kill-pane is idempotent/best-effort so a double-invoke on the audit paths is harmless, but avoid redundant enumerated calls once the single exit exists. Gotchas: paneCountMutex (src/tmux/session.ts:273) returns 'available' only at exactly 2 panes, so a lingering plan pane = 3 = busy. Do NOT regress CAM-188 (worker/reviewer teardown at finishTerminal) or CAM-204. Tests live in test/supervisor/plan/plan-runner-replan.test.ts (unit, seam-injected) and test/supervisor/plan/plan-sidecar-replan-wiring.test.ts (wiring). No vendor/templates or Ink touched.
